title: Tool detection and GitHub identity: Claude Code and gh installed and signed in, login, name and email, guidance text
story: Grillo's main process now checks whether Claude Code and the GitHub command-line tool are installed and signed in, and reads who the member is on GitHub. Two new channels, tools:check and tools:identity, feed the setup screen that comes later. There is no screen yet, and nothing earlier was replaced.

checks.criterion: Grillo reports Claude Code and gh as installed and signed in, with versions and no guidance
checks.steps: On a laptop where claude and gh are installed and signed in, start Grillo with npm run dev. In the developer tools console run: await window.grillo.invoke('tools:check', {})
checks.expected: Both tools installed and signed in, each with a version number; guidance is null.

checks.criterion: A signed-out tool gets the exact sign-in command
checks.steps: Run gh auth logout, then in the console: await window.grillo.invoke('tools:check', { force: true })
checks.expected: gh shows signed in false, with guidance { action: 'sign-in', command: 'gh auth login --web' }.

checks.criterion: Results are cached for 10 seconds; a forced check asks again
checks.steps: After signing gh back in, call tools:check with {} within 10 seconds of the previous check, then with { force: true }.
checks.expected: The first call still shows the old signed-out result; the forced call shows signed in.

checks.criterion: Grillo reads the GitHub login, name and email, and reports a signed-out gh as a typed result
checks.steps: Run await window.grillo.invoke('tools:identity', undefined) while signed in, then again after gh auth logout.
checks.expected: First { ok: true, identity: { login, name, email } } (email may be null), then { ok: false, reason: 'signed-out' }.
